draft.title: Sleep as a state of consciousness
card: Consciousness is awareness of yourself, your thoughts and your surroundings. It can change in level, from fully alert to deeply asleep.
An altered state of consciousness (ASC) is any state that differs from normal waking consciousness. Sleep is one ASC, and it happens naturally without drugs or other outside help.
In sleep, awareness of surroundings is reduced. A sleeper may still react to strong sounds or touch, but far less than when awake.
Brain activity also changes in sleep. Brain waves differ from those of an alert waking brain, and they change as the night goes on.
draft.remember: Sleep is a natural altered state: less awareness of surroundings, and different brain activity.

a.q: Why is sleep classed as an altered state of consciousness?
opts: It differs from waking in awareness and brain activity
It is caused by drugs that lower awareness of surroundings
It involves no brain activity, so awareness stops completely
It is a state a person must learn to enter on purpose
a.why: Sleep differs from normal waking consciousness in awareness and in brain activity. The drug option is wrong because sleep is natural, and the no-activity option is wrong because the brain stays active and its waves change.
a.clue: Compare sleep with normal waking consciousness.

b.q: Tane falls asleep on the train home to Geelong and does not notice the other passengers getting on. Which feature of sleep does this best show?
opts: A state brought on by outside help
Full awareness of his own thoughts
b.why: Not noticing the passengers shows that his awareness of his surroundings has fallen, which is a feature of sleep as an altered state. Brain activity does not stop in sleep. It changes.
b.clue: Think about what Tane is no longer aware of.

a.best: It differs from waking in awareness and brain activity
